chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Tha'laba, from Abu al-Hasan Umar ibn Shaddad al-Azdi and al-Sarri, both together, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man has greater right over his wealth for as long as the soul remains within him. If he were to bequeath the whole of it, it is permissible for him.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: has greater right (superlative of haqq — right/entitlement); indicates priority claim
key_terms.أَوْصَى: bequeathed/willed; refers to the act of making a wasiyya (last will and testament)
key_terms.الرُّوحُ: the soul/spirit; its presence in the body signifies the person is still alive
key_terms.جَائِزٌ: permissible/valid; a technical legal term in fiqh indicating something is allowed

ai.seo_question: Does a person have the right to bequeath all their wealth in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the absolute right of a living person to dispose of all his wealth, including through bequest (wasiyya) of the entire estate. This ruling addresses a fundamental question in Islamic inheritance law: whether a dying person's freedom to distribute his wealth is limited by the prescribed shares of heirs. The Imam's ruling, while permitting a bequest of the whole estate during one's lifetime, operates within the broader fiqh context of testamentary limits that scholars discuss.
